unlisted_practices: Adopt interoperability standards end-to-end: DICOM for imaging objects, HL7 FHIR for clinical APIs, and IHE profiles for operational workflows.
Define a minimum semantic rule set (laterality, anatomy, indication), bind it to controlled terminologies such as RadLex and SNOMED CT, and run periodic semantic audits.
Define and enforce a minimum interoperability dataset and minimum metadata capture at ingestion, with protocol naming and versioning and automated QC checks.
Establish cross-site governance for patient identity, procedure catalogs, and protocol versioning, with end-to-end integration testing.
Use structured reporting for high-impact pathways, keep templates concise, and auto-populate quantitative fields.
Enable radiomics reproducibility through acquisition harmonization and IBSI-aligned feature pipelines.
Build interdisciplinary teams including radiologists, technologists, physicists, IT, clinical engineers, and data stewards, and invest in change management.
Follow AI reporting frameworks such as CONSORT-AI, SPIRIT-AI, and TRIPOD+AI when evaluating and communicating AI tools.
Implement integration layers with documented interfaces and end-to-end testing to address legacy IT fragmentation and vendor lock-in.
Provide interpretable AI outputs with uncertainty cues and links to supporting evidence.
